offensivePositionsDiagram.hint: Click a player in the formation.
offensivePositionsDiagram.qbBlurb: The brains of the offense — decides every play.
offensivePositionsDiagram.rbBlurb: Runs with the ball, gains yards on the ground.
offensivePositionsDiagram.wrBlurb: Catches passes out on the edges.
offensivePositionsDiagram.teBlurb: A hybrid: blocks and catches passes.
offensivePositionsDiagram.olBlurb: Protects the quarterback, opens running lanes.

defensivePositionsDiagram.hint: Click a player in the formation.
defensivePositionsDiagram.dlBlurb: Stops the run and pressures the quarterback.
defensivePositionsDiagram.lbBlurb: Versatile — stop runs, cover passes, blitz the quarterback.
defensivePositionsDiagram.sBlurb: The last line of defense — prevents the deep pass.

routeTreeDiagram.hint: Click a number to see the route.
routeTreeDiagram.route0Blurb: A short route to the sideline, near the line of scrimmage.
routeTreeDiagram.route1Blurb: A quick, sharp cut inside at a shallow angle.
routeTreeDiagram.route2Blurb: A few yards upfield, then breaks toward the sideline.
routeTreeDiagram.route3Blurb: Runs upfield, then turns back toward the quarterback.
routeTreeDiagram.route4Blurb: A longer route, then a sharp break back toward the sideline.
routeTreeDiagram.route5Blurb: Medium-to-long distance, then breaks toward the sideline.
routeTreeDiagram.route6Blurb: Medium-to-long distance, then a hard cut across the middle.
routeTreeDiagram.route7Blurb: A deep route breaking toward the corner of the field.
routeTreeDiagram.route8Blurb: A deep route breaking toward the middle of the field.
routeTreeDiagram.route9Blurb: A straight sprint as far downfield as possible.

situationalFootballDiagram.hint: Pick a scenario to see the context that changes the decision.
situationalFootballDiagram.twoMinuteSummary: No huddle, sideline passes to stop the clock, timeouts spent with surgical precision.
situationalFootballDiagram.twoMinuteChange1: The clock becomes the opponent, not just the defense
situationalFootballDiagram.twoMinuteChange2: Any play that doesn't stop the clock costs real time
situationalFootballDiagram.twoMinuteChange3: Timeouts are worth as much as a successful play
situationalFootballDiagram.fourthDownSummary: Risk it for possession, or play it safe with a punt? Modern analytics say to go for it more often than instinct suggests.
situationalFootballDiagram.fourthDownChange1: Field position decides whether a failed attempt is catastrophic or just inconvenient
situationalFootballDiagram.fourthDownChange2: The score changes a team's appetite for risk
situationalFootballDiagram.fourthDownChange3: Time remaining limits how many more tries you get
situationalFootballDiagram.redZoneSummary: The field compresses, deep passes disappear — the gap between 7 and 3 points is decided here.
situationalFootballDiagram.redZoneChange1: The space behind the defense disappears completely
situationalFootballDiagram.redZoneChange2: Every yard is contested at close range
situationalFootballDiagram.redZoneChange3: A missed touchdown here means only 3 points, not 7
situationalFootballDiagram.clockMgmtSummary: The team in the lead wants the clock running — runs that stay in bounds are worth more than the yards themselves.
situationalFootballDiagram.clockMgmtChange1: Every second that ticks away is an advantage earned without another snap
situationalFootballDiagram.clockMgmtChange2: Going out of bounds stops the clock and helps the opponent
situationalFootballDiagram.clockMgmtChange3: The opponent's timeouts become the real limited resource
situationalFootballDiagram.kneelDownSummary: Nothing spectacular — the quarterback takes a knee, the clock runs out, the game ends safely.
situationalFootballDiagram.kneelDownChange1: Any real play introduces the risk of a fumble or an injury
situationalFootballDiagram.kneelDownChange2: The win is already mathematically certain — there's no upside left
situationalFootballDiagram.kneelDownChange3: It symbolically marks the end of the game before the final whistle

boxScoreDiagram.widgetLabel: Interactive diagram: how to read a box score
boxScoreDiagram.hint: Tap an element to see what it means.
boxScoreDiagram.scoreBugBlurb: The bar up top summarizes the game: the two teams and the current score. One glance and you know exactly where the game stands.
boxScoreDiagram.gameClockBlurb: Shows the current quarter and the time left in it. Each quarter is 15 minutes of game time, but the clock stops often — so a quarter takes much longer in real time.
boxScoreDiagram.downDistanceBlurb: "3RD & 4": which down it is, and how many yards are left for a new first down. Without it you can't tell whether the offense is succeeding or about to turn the ball over.
boxScoreDiagram.fieldPositionBlurb: "KC 36" means the ball is on KC's own 36-yard line. On screen, the position is also marked with a black line on the field — the line of scrimmage, right where the previous play ended. Combined with down & distance, it tells you exactly how close the offense is to scoring or to losing possession.
boxScoreDiagram.timeoutsBlurb: Each team gets 3 timeouts per half — they stop the clock instantly, on demand. Teams spend them carefully, especially in the final minutes, when stopping the clock can matter more than any play. In the example above, NE only has 2 left — it already used one earlier in the half.
boxScoreDiagram.playClockBlurb: Counts down from 40 (or 25). It's how much time the offense has left to snap the ball. When it nears zero and the team hasn't moved, expect either a rushed play or a delay-of-game penalty.
boxScoreDiagram.firstDownLineBlurb: The target line — the yellow line you see on screen — shows exactly where the offense needs to reach for a new first down. It's drawn in digitally; it doesn't exist on the actual field, but it makes the game instantly readable.

statLinesDiagram.widgetLabel: Interactive diagram: how to read a stat line
statLinesDiagram.hint: Tap a position to see what it means.
statLinesDiagram.passingBlurb: A quarterback's line: how many passes completed out of how many attempted (CMP/ATT), how many yards thrown, how many touchdowns, and how many interceptions.
statLinesDiagram.rushingBlurb: A running back's line: how many times he carried the ball (CAR), how many yards he gained, and how many touchdowns he scored on the ground.
statLinesDiagram.receivingBlurb: A receiver's line: how many passes he caught (REC), how many total yards he gained, and how many touchdowns he scored.
